issues.description: Field mismatch for Animal.name: the problem statement explicitly instructs that the Animal.name attribute should be implemented using java.lang.StringBuilder to allow efficient string manipulations, but the reference solution declares the field as a String (private String name) and provides a String-based constructor/getter/setter. This discrepancy (problem_statement.md vs. src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) creates confusion for students about the intended attribute type and the expected constructor/getter/setter signatures and semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Preferred fix (align implementation to the problem statement): change the Animal implementation to use a StringBuilder backing field while keeping a convenient String-based API to minimize changes required in subclasses/tests. Example: private StringBuilder name; public Animal(String name) { this.name = new StringBuilder(name); } public String getName() { return name.toString(); } public void setName(String newName) { this.name.setLength(0); this.name.append(newName); } Update any subclass code if it depends on the concrete field type. Alternative fix (align problem statement to implementation): update the problem statement to require a String for name instead of StringBuilder and clarify expected getter/setter types. Choose one approach and update tests/documentation accordingly so students have an unambiguous single specification.
